body.statement: Suppose \(G_n\to\infty\), \(p_n\to p\in(0,1)\), and \(N_n/n\to\rho\in(0,1]\). Under either \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}}\) or \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}\), the unit-permutation-then-label-permutation predictable variation satisfies, jointly over the prior and design, \[ G_nQ_n\xrightarrow{L^2} \begin{cases} [Mp(1-p)]^{-1},&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}},\\ [Mp(1-p)]^{-1}-2\rho/M,&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}. \end{cases} \] Consequently, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), under either prior, \[ \mathbb P_{\mathbb H_n}\!\left\{ \mathbb P_{\mathbf A_n,\mathbf Z_n}\!\left( \left|Q_n/\sigma_n^2-1\right|>\varepsilon\mid Y\right)>\varepsilon \right\}\longrightarrow0. \]
body.proof_tex:
For either prior, introduce unit-level arm values \(X_{i1}\) and \(X_{i0}\) by
\[
(X_{i1},X_{i0})=
\begin{cases}
(U_i,U_i),&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}},\\
(U_i,V_i),&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}},
\end{cases}
\qquad d_i=X_{i1}-X_{i0},
\]
where the displayed signs are independent Rademacher variables except for the equality imposed under \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}}\).  These priors give the additive schedules
\[
h_{z,n}(A)=\frac1M\sum_{i\in A}X_{iz},
\qquad
\tau_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n d_i.                                      \tag{1}
\]
All expectations in the calculation below are joint over the indicated prior and the two-stage design unless conditioning is displayed.  Write \(G=G_n\), \(N=N_n\), and \(q_n=1-p_n\).  Assumption~\ref{ass:stable-treatment-fraction} supplies a constant \(\delta>0\) such that \(p_n,q_n\geq\delta\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).

We first split the Doob martingale at the end of the unit-permutation reveal.  Given the realized blocks, complete randomization of the labels gives
\[
\mathbb E[\widehat\tau_n\mid\mathbf A_n]
=\frac1G\sum_{g=1}^G\{h_{1,n}(A_{ng})-h_{0,n}(A_{ng})\}
=\frac1N\sum_{r=1}^N d_{U_r}.
\]
For
\[
c_g=\frac{h_{1,n}(A_{ng})}{p_n}
    +\frac{h_{0,n}(A_{ng})}{q_n},
\]
direct subtraction of this conditional mean from the estimator in Definition~\ref{def:pame-estimator} gives
\[
\widehat\tau_n-\mathbb E[\widehat\tau_n\mid\mathbf A_n]
=\frac1G\sum_{g=1}^G(Z_{ng}-p_n)c_g.                                  \tag{2}
\]
Because the unit permutation is revealed completely before any label and the label permutation is independent of it by Definition~\ref{def:random-partition-design}, equations (1)--(2) decompose the predictable variation as
\[
Q_n=Q_n^U+Q_n^L,                                                       \tag{3}
\]
where the superscripts denote the unit- and label-reveal phases.

Let \(L_n=n-N\).  Just before unit reveal \(r\), let \(\mu_{r-1}^d\) and
\[
v_{r-1}^d=\frac1{n-r+1}\sum_{i\ {\rm remaining}}
                 (d_i-\mu_{r-1}^d)^2
\]
be the mean and denominator-population variance of the remaining values.  When \(N<n\), subtracting the conditional expected sample mean before and after reveal \(r\) yields
\[
D_{n,r}^U=\frac{L_n}{N(n-r)}(d_{U_r}-\mu_{r-1}^d),
\qquad
Q_n^U=\sum_{r=1}^{N}\frac{L_n^2}{N^2(n-r)^2}v_{r-1}^d.                 \tag{4}
\]
When \(N=n\), the selected-sample mean equals the population mean identically, so \(Q_n^U=0\).

Under \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}}\), every \(d_i=0\), hence \(Q_n^U=0\).  Under \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}\), the randomly permuted \(d_i\)'s are independent, have mean zero, variance two, and satisfy \(|d_i|\leq2\).  For a remaining population of size \(m\), expansion of its empirical first and second moments and Cauchy--Schwarz give
\[
\mathbb E|v_{r-1}^d-2|\leq C m^{-1/2},
\qquad m=n-r+1,                                                       \tag{5}
\]
for a universal finite constant \(C\).  Define the deterministic coefficient sum
\[
S_n
=G\sum_{r=1}^{N}\frac{L_n^2}{N^2(n-r)^2}
=\frac{L_n^2}{MN}\sum_{j=L_n}^{n-1}j^{-2},                            \tag{6}
\]
when \(L_n\geq1\), and put \(S_n=0\) when \(L_n=0\).  If \(0<\rho<1\), the integral comparison for the decreasing function \(x^{-2}\), together with \(N/n\to\rho\), gives
\[
S_n\longrightarrow\frac{1-\rho}{M}.                                  \tag{7}
\]
Moreover, every remaining population in (4) has size at least \(L_n+1\asymp n\); hence (5) and (6) imply
\[
\mathbb E|GQ_n^U-2S_n|
\leq C(L_n+1)^{-1/2}S_n\longrightarrow0.                              \tag{8}
\]
If \(\rho=1\) and \(L_n\geq1\), another integral comparison gives
\[
0\leq S_n
\leq\frac{L_n^2}{MN}\left(\frac1{L_n^2}+\frac1{L_n}\right)
=\frac{1+L_n}{MN}\longrightarrow0,                                   \tag{9}
\]
because \(L_n/n\to0\) and \(N/n\to1\).  The bound \(v_{r-1}^d\leq4\) then makes \(GQ_n^U\leq4S_n\to0\).  Equations (7)--(9) prove
\[
GQ_n^U\xrightarrow{L^1}
\begin{cases}
0,&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}},\\
2(1-\rho)/M,&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}.
\end{cases}                                                           \tag{10}
\]

We next reveal the labels.  Just before label \(s\), let
\[
\pi_{s-1}=\frac{G_{1n}-\sum_{j<s}Z_{nj}}{G-s+1},
\qquad
\bar c_{s+1:G}=\frac1{G-s}\sum_{j>s}c_j.
\]
Taking successive conditional expectations in (2) gives, for \(s<G\),
\[
D_{n,N+s}^L
=\frac{Z_{ns}-\pi_{s-1}}G(c_s-\bar c_{s+1:G}),                       \tag{11}
\]
while the final label is determined and has zero increment.  Therefore
\[
GQ_n^L
=\frac1G\sum_{s=1}^{G-1}\pi_{s-1}(1-\pi_{s-1})
                  (c_s-\bar c_{s+1:G})^2.                             \tag{12}
\]
The label process is independent of \((c_1,\ldots,c_G)\).  If \(K=G-s+1\) labels remain, elementary sampling-without-replacement covariance algebra gives
\[
\mathbb E(\pi_{s-1}-p_n)^2
=p_nq_n\frac{G-K}{K(G-1)}.                                            \tag{13}
\]
Since \(|x(1-x)-p_nq_n|\leq2|x-p_n|\), since \(|c_g|\leq p_n^{-1}+q_n^{-1}\leq2/\delta\), and since \(G^{-1}\sum_{K=2}^G K^{-1/2}=O(G^{-1/2})\), equations (12)--(13) and Cauchy--Schwarz imply
\[
GQ_n^L-\frac{p_nq_n}{G}\sum_{s=1}^{G-1}
                    (c_s-\bar c_{s+1:G})^2\xrightarrow{L^1}0.         \tag{14}
\]

Under either prior, the disjoint blocks use disjoint collections of independent signs.  Consequently, jointly over the unit permutation and the prior, \(c_1,\ldots,c_G\) are independent and identically distributed, centered, and uniformly bounded.  The reverse updating identity
\[
\sum_{s=1}^{G-1}\frac{G-s}{G-s+1}(c_s-\bar c_{s+1:G})^2
=\sum_{g=1}^{G}(c_g-\bar c)^2                                        \tag{15}
\]
follows by expanding the two sides recursively.  The absolute difference between the unweighted sum in (14) and the left side of (15) is at most
\[
4(2/\delta)^2\sum_{K=2}^G K^{-1}=O(\log G).                           \tag{16}
\]
The bounded triangular-array law of large numbers applied to the right side of (15), together with (16) and Assumption~\ref{ass:group-count-growth}, now gives
\[
\frac1G\sum_{s=1}^{G-1}(c_s-\bar c_{s+1:G})^2
-\operatorname{Var}(c_1)\xrightarrow{L^2}0.                           \tag{17}
\]
Direct calculation from (1) gives
\[
\operatorname{Var}(c_1)=
\begin{cases}
[Mp_n^2q_n^2]^{-1},&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}},\\
M^{-1}(p_n^{-2}+q_n^{-2}),&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}.
\end{cases}                                                           \tag{18}
\]
Equations (12)--(18) and \(p_n\to p\), \(q_n\to q=1-p\), prove
\[
GQ_n^L\xrightarrow{L^1}
\begin{cases}
[Mpq]^{-1},&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}},\\
M^{-1}(q/p+p/q),&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}.
\end{cases}                                                           \tag{19}
\]

The coefficient sum \(S_n\) is at most \(1/M\), because (6) contains \(N\) summands, each at most \(L_n^{-2}\).  Thus (4) implies \(GQ_n^U\leq4/M\).  Equation (12) and the uniform bound on \(c_g\) likewise give a deterministic constant bounding \(GQ_n^L\).  Hence the \(L^1\) convergences in (10) and (19) upgrade to \(L^2\) convergence.  Adding them and using
\[
\frac qp+\frac pq+2=\frac1{pq}
\]
establishes
\[
G_nQ_n\xrightarrow{L^2}
\begin{cases}
[Mp(1-p)]^{-1},&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}},\\
[Mp(1-p)]^{-1}-2\rho/M,&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}.
\end{cases}                                                           \tag{20}
\]
In particular, \(\operatorname{Var}(G_nQ_n)\to0\), which is the required normalized predictable-variation check.

Because the proposed scope has \(\rho>0\), Proposition~\ref{prop:rademacher-mixture-separation} applies and gives convergence in prior probability of \(G_n\sigma_n^2\) to the same respective constants.  Both constants are positive: the independent-prior constant is at least \(2/M\), since \(p(1-p)\leq1/4\) and \(\rho\leq1\).  Equation (20) and division by a random denominator bounded away from zero in probability therefore give
\[
Q_n/\sigma_n^2\xrightarrow{p}1                                      \tag{21}
\]
jointly over prior and design.  For fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), put
\[
b_n(Y)=\mathbb P_{\mathbf A_n,\mathbf Z_n}
\left(\left.|Q_n/\sigma_n^2-1|>\varepsilon\,\right|Y\right).
\]
By iterated expectation, (21) says \(\mathbb E_{\mathbb H_n}b_n(Y)\to0\).  Markov's inequality then yields
\[
\mathbb P_{\mathbb H_n}\{b_n(Y)>\varepsilon\}
\leq\varepsilon^{-1}\mathbb E_{\mathbb H_n}b_n(Y)\longrightarrow0,
\]
which is the final assertion.
body.justification: The exact unit-then-label reveal calculation verifies the filtration premise on the two additive Rademacher prior supports and proves \(\operatorname{Var}(G_nQ_n)=o(1)\); it is not a general bounded-schedule theorem.
body.gap: The lemma is restricted to \(\rho\in(0,1]\), matching both the variance-limit proposition it invokes and the positive-density impossibility theorem that consumes it.
body.consumer: It certifies high-prior-probability deterministic support sets with predictable-variation stability for the diagonal lower bound, independently of ambient-class membership.
